document.title: Gameplan for Polmil Strategy for Pakistan and Afghanistan
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), New Documents Detail America's Strategic Response to 9/11
document.note: [Secret/NODIS] Since the attacks show UBL can conduct terrorism under Taliban control, State proposes demands on the Taliban (surrender al-Qaeda associates, provide intelligence, expel terrorists), subtle ways to encourage splits in Taliban leadership, and use of force if the deadline is missed. It stresses coordination with Pakistan, the Central Asian states, Russia and possibly Iran; Pakistan will not send troops into Afghanistan but will give other support.

events.description: Tuesday's terrorist attacks on the US, attributed to UBL and al-Qa'ida, which prompt the US demands on the Taliban
State Department gameplan sets out demands on the Taliban (turn over UBL and deputies, close camps, free SNI workers), deadlines of 24-48 hours, and penalties and options for noncompliance
Tuesday's attacks demonstrate UBL's capability to conduct terrorism while under Taliban control.
Proposed ultimatum: Taliban given 24-48 hours to turn over UBL and chief lieutenants and close camps.
Planned consultations with Pakistan, Saudis, UAE, P-5, NATO allies, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Russia, India and possibly Iran begin immediately.
Option One: M-Day message to Taliban with deadlines of 24-48 hours for reply, 72 hours for action to begin, 10-14 days to carry out operation; Option Three planning begins M+3.

key_claims: The US judged that the 11 September attacks showed UBL could conduct terrorism while under Taliban control, contrary to repeated Taliban assurances.
The US demanded the Taliban hand over UBL and deputies Zawahiri, Atef and Abu Zubaidah, close camps and free SNI workers.
The plan proposed Pakistan carry the message to the Taliban leadership in Kandahar, with parallel delivery via the US Embassy Islamabad.
If the Taliban refused, the US would work to remove the Taliban leadership from power, backing a Northern Alliance-based coalition and striking Taliban military targets.
The US urged Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Pakistan to break relations with the Taliban and to detain or expel Taliban representatives abroad.
The US assessed that Pakistan would be unwilling to send troops into Afghanistan but would provide other operational and logistical support.
